main_diagnosis: With neg_avg_log_marginal_NLE=22.1, the model is poorly fitting observed tonic-spiking statistics. The primary failure mode is progressive I_M (w-gate) accumulation during tonic firing: V_half_w=-35 mV causes w to surge toward 1.0 during each AP (V far exceeds -35 mV), and with tau_w floored at 20 ms plus ISIs of 20–50 ms, w never returns to its inter-spike steady-state (~0.076 at -50 mV) before the next spike. After 3–5 spikes, w plateaus near 0.4–0.6, delivering gbar_M×0.5×30 ≈ 30 µA/cm² of chronic outward current — systematically suppressing spike count (stat 1), lowering mean stimulation voltage (stat 4), and distorting higher-order moments (stats 6–7). The secondary issue is that gbar_A ceiling of 1.0 mS/cm² combined with b_inf(-65)=0.5 initial condition creates a transient I_A outward pulse at stimulus onset (before b inactivates) that can delay or suppress the first spike, introducing asymmetry in spike timing not present in the data.

issues.description: Progressive I_M w-gate accumulation during tonic spiking. During each AP, V exceeds -35 mV by 60–80 mV, driving w_inf toward 1.0. With tau_w in [20, 80] ms and typical ISIs of 20–50 ms, w decays only ~22–63% between spikes. After 5+ spikes, w plateaus near 0.4–0.7, producing chronic inter-spike I_M ≈ gbar_M × 0.5 × 30 ≈ 30 µA/cm² at maximum gbar_M=2.0. This is functionally equivalent to the 'tonic suppression' pathology that V_half_w=-45 mV was corrected to avoid, but now occurring via AP-peak w-accumulation rather than subthreshold activation. The result is underestimated spike count (stat 1), reduced mean stimulation voltage (stat 4), and heavy-tailed voltage distribution (stats 6–7).
issues.location: w_inf_M, tau_w, gbar_M mapping — lines defining V_half_w=-35, tau_w=20+60*sigmoid(...), and gbar_M=2.0*(p/120)
issues.suggestion: Shift V_half_w from -35 mV to -20 mV so that w_inf at the AP peak (~+40 mV) remains ~0.999 but w_inf at subthreshold/ISI voltages (-50 mV) drops from 0.076 to ~0.004, reducing inter-spike w accumulation by ~19×. Simultaneously reduce gbar_M ceiling from 2.0 to 1.0 mS/cm² (change mapping to 1.0*(p/120)) to limit total post-spike I_M. These two changes together ensure that even after full w accumulation, inter-spike I_M ≤ 1.0×0.4×30 = 12 µA/cm² — providing genuine spike-rate adaptation without tonic suppression. Alternatively, raise the tau_w floor from 20 ms to 60 ms to slow accumulation across spikes, preventing w from reaching a plateau before the stimulus ends.

issues.description: I_A onset transient from b_inf(-65)=0.5 initial condition. At simulation start (V=-65 mV), b=0.5 (half-inactivated). When stimulus arrives and V depolarizes, a_inf rises rapidly (instantaneous gate), so I_A = gbar_A × a^3 × 0.5 fires a large outward pulse before b can inactivate further. At gbar_A=1.0 mS/cm² and a_inf(-40)=0.5: I_A ≈ 1.0 × 0.125 × 0.5 × 30 = 1.9 µA/cm² outward burst. This first-spike delay is absent from subsequent spikes (b recovers to only ~0.84 at AHP bottom, then reinactivates), creating a non-uniform ISI distribution inconsistent with the evenly-spaced tonic spiking in the data — distorting skewness (stat 6) and kurtosis (stat 7) of the voltage distribution.
issues.location: b[:, 0] = b_inf_A(V[:, 0]) initialization and a_inf_A computation with V_half_b=-65 mV
issues.suggestion: Shift V_half_b from -65 mV to -55 mV so that b_inf at rest (-65 mV) = 1/(1+exp((-65+55)/6)) = 1/(1+exp(-1.67)) ≈ 0.84 rather than 0.5. This means I_A starts near its fully-recovered state at rest (b≈0.84), matching the expectation that the b gate is mostly de-inactivated at hyperpolarized resting potential. The first-spike I_A pulse becomes similar in magnitude to subsequent spikes (b recovers to ~0.84 after each AHP, matching the IC), eliminating the asymmetric onset transient. Per-spike I_A outward pulse is then symmetric across the spike train, producing the regular ISI structure consistent with tonic spiking (stats 1, 6, 7 improved).
